pre_event_feedback:
To further strengthen the experience for both vendors and attendees, I would like to propose a few ideas around layout, visibility, and collaboration for future events.

A clearly communicated layout ahead of the festival would be highly beneficial, particularly for non-food vendors. From experience, customer flow naturally gravitates toward food and beverage, as these are essential purchases. Fashion and lifestyle vendors, however, rely on discovery and impulse. Positioning non-food vendors along the main walkways leading toward food areas would ensure consistent foot traffic and increased exposure, allowing customers to engage with these offerings before reaching food and drink destinations.

In addition, a more intentional traffic flow, guiding attendees through non-essential vendors en route to essential ones would significantly enhance trading opportunities. Many festival-goers are simply unaware of the full range of vendors available, and thoughtful placement can make a substantial difference.

From a marketing perspective, there is also an opportunity to strengthen collaboration. Sharing all participating vendors across Bazique’s social media platforms, and tagging or collaborating on posts, would allow for meaningful cross-pollination and increased reach in the lead-up to the event.

Flock would be very interested in contributing to this from our side as well. With our new store in the Cape Town CBD, we could support ticket sales as a physical partner location, as well as display posters or marketing material in-store to help drive awareness and can even do a pre Bazique event . We also have an engaged local and international customer base through our newsletter, which we could activate with direct booking links to further support ticket sales.

Additionally, we would love to explore collaborative marketing initiatives such as competitions or giveaways offering, for example, event tickets paired with curated Flock outfits to build excitement and engagement ahead of the festival.

We believe there is strong potential to grow this partnership in a way that benefits both the festival and its vendors, and we would be excited to explore these opportunities further.

onsite_feedback:
The single biggest difference to our on-site experience would have been reliable WiFi, supported by clear and consistent communication from the team during the outage.

As a non-food vendor, our ability to trade is entirely dependent on connectivity. The downtime during peak trading hours directly impacted sales and customer experience. However, the lack of updates and check-ins during this period amplified the issue, leaving me, my team and our customers uncertain and frustrated.

In addition to this, a more intentional vendor layout and traffic flow would have significantly improved our experience. Positioning non-food vendors along key pathways leading to food and beverage areas would ensure consistent visibility and engagement, as customers naturally move toward essential purchases.

An additional improvement that would make a meaningful difference is access to dedicated vendor toilets and shower facilities. This would ensure that both we and our staff can prepare efficiently and remain presentable throughout the event, without needing to queue for extended periods or travel far from our trading space.

Together, reliable infrastructure, proactive communication, and strategic layout planning would have made the most meaningful impact on our overall trading experience.
comms_style: Generally good but could be more proactive
vm_feedback:
Clear, proactive communication would significantly improve vendor management, particularly during operational challenges. Regular check-ins and real-time updates (especially around critical infrastructure like WiFi) are essential to ensure vendors can manage both their teams and customer expectations effectively.

The event started off very communicative, and the team was helpful and present. However, once the WiFi went down, communication dropped entirely. There were no check-ins with me or my team, and I had to walk around to find information, only to repeatedly be told that it would be back up “soon,” with no clear timeline or updates until late.

This lack of clarity made it difficult to manage customer expectations. We communicated the same message to clients, many of whom returned multiple times to try complete their purchases, only to eventually leave after continued delays.

In addition, having a clearly communicated layout and vendor strategy ahead of the event would allow for better preparation. Thoughtful placement of non-food vendors along key traffic routes, supported by intentional flow design, would improve visibility and trading outcomes.

Stronger pre-event and on-site coordination, combined with collaborative marketing efforts that include all vendors would elevate both the vendor experience and overall event success.
improvements_2027: Better foot traffic past stalls, Improved power infrastructure, Guaranteed connectivity for payments, Fewer vendors (less competition), Premium stall placement for an additional fee, More pre-event marketing to festivalgoers, I wouldn’t necessarily recommend increasing the number of non-essential vendors. Instead, I would strongly suggest focusing on quality over quantity.  A carefully curated selection of vendors, with an emphasis on originality, craftsmanship, and overall presentation, will elevate the entire festival experience. Ensuring a high standard across all offerings not only strengthens the visual identity of the event but also enhances customer perception and spending.  A well-balanced, hand-selected vendor mix will ultimately be more impactful than a larger, less curated market.

marketplace_thoughts:
We would definitely be interested in participating, this has strong potential to extend vendor revenue beyond the physical event and improve overall customer experience.

A few thoughts that would make the marketplace truly effective:

Pre-event browsing with “reserve & collect” or pre-purchase options would be highly valuable. This allows customers to secure items ahead of time and reduces missed sales during busy trading periods or infrastructure challenges.

Post-event sales extension - where to find who (e.g. 3–7 days after the festival) would help capture customers who discovered brands at the event but didn’t complete purchases on-site. Inclusion into marketing emails if professional content is provided.

Vendor control over branding and pricing is essential. Each brand should feel like their own store within the platform, maintaining identity and perceived value.

A simple, reliable payment system is critical to ensure a seamless customer experience.

Clear logistics around shipping vs. collection, with defined responsibilities, will be important for operational ease.

Strong marketing integration will ultimately drive success, this includes promotion before, during, and after the event, with vendor collaboration and shared visibility.

Access to data and insights (sales, traffic, customer behaviour) would be extremely valuable for vendors to evaluate performance and plan ahead.

In addition to the marketplace, Flock would be keen to explore a pre-event in-store activation for locally made clothing and accessory brands participating in the festival. We have a new 150sqm retail space in the Cape Town CBD and could host a Bazique-aligned activation as part of a First Thursday ahead of the event.

This would create an opportunity to build hype, introduce customers to the brands before the festival, and drive early engagement. We would be open to working on a participation fee structure, and it would be important that this is a Bazique-approved initiative, supported and marketed collaboratively across all channels.

If executed well, both the marketplace and pre-event activation could significantly enhance vendor profitability, customer experience, and overall festival momentum. We’d be excited to be part of shaping and supporting this.
other_feedback:
We approach festivals as a core part of our business, not as a casual or promotional opportunity. Flock is a VAT-registered company with a fully operational retail store and e-commerce platform, and we take our trading very seriously.

Over the years, we have intentionally scaled down the number of festivals we attend, choosing to participate only in those that are well-aligned with our brand and commercially viable. Each event is a considered investment for us.

We arrive with a full team, not only to manage sales, but also to create high-quality content that contributes to both our brand and the overall festival visibility. Our presence is structured, strategic, and focused on delivering strong results.

It would be great to explore more aligned collaboration opportunities where there is mutual value. For example, we would be grateful to be considered for an additional one or two tickets for our team where relevant. This could be a vetted process ahead of the event, based on a clear plan and purpose (and not necessarily extended to all vendors), ensuring it remains structured and beneficial to both parties.
